summary: Completed full backend testing of HRMS Reporting Module Phase A. All 5 endpoints (analytics, salary-register, salary-slip-pdf, attendance, pool-distribution) tested with 16 pytest cases covering HTTP codes, file content parsing (openpyxl + %PDF signature), headers, and validation edge cases. 16/16 PASSED. File contents verified structurally (not just status codes) — salary register has full CTC breakup + deductions + employer contributions + TOTAL row, pool distribution aggregates PRC per employee with TOTAL row (0.1373 PRC confirmed for EMP-0001 on 2026-04-19), attendance Excel has 30-day matrix, analytics JSON contains all 7 top-level sections.

minor.issue: Attendance percentage denominator is hardcoded to 26 (eff/26*100) — should use days_in_month minus holidays or a configurable working-days value. Minor cosmetic/accuracy issue.
counts['holiday'] is tracked in the loop but never written into the per-row summary columns. 'O' code cells are rendered in-grid so likely intentional, but report a Holiday column may be useful.
No auth guard on reports endpoints. Context note marks this acceptable for MVP, but should be protected before production.

action_items: (Optional) Replace hardcoded /26 in attendance percent calc with days_in_month - holidays.
(Optional) Add Holiday column to attendance summary if intended.
(Pre-prod) Add auth/role guard to /api/employees/reports/* before launch.
critical_code_review_comments: employee_reports.py is 879 lines — approaching the 700-line threshold; consider splitting by report (salary_register.py, salary_slip_pdf.py, attendance.py, pool.py, analytics.py) for maintainability.
Attendance percentage formula hardcodes /26 — extract as constant WORKING_DAYS_DEFAULT or compute from days_in_month.
Pool distribution uses string timestamp comparison — relies on ISO format; would be safer to parse datetimes.
Good: all endpoints properly return StreamingResponse with correct media types and Content-Disposition headers.
Good: Pydantic/Query validators (ge=1, le=12 on month, ge=2020 le=2100 on year) produce proper 422 responses.
Good: 404 correctly raised for non-existent employee_id in salary-slip-pdf.
